newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish bonds market closed down on Monday, but off lows as profit-taking emerged before Tuesday's auction on five and 10-year government bonds.

"The market was making room for the new issues," a trader in Madrid said. The Treasury should see a very good demand based on market conditions, possibly setting a historical record for the 10-year yield below the eight percent level, dealers said.

The 10-year 8.80 percent bond, which will be sold on Tuesday was down in late trade at 105.46 from 105.69 earlier. The December futures contract was trading at 106.22, down 60 basis points from Friday's close, after a low at 106.14.

Earlier on Monday the Treasury forecast it would issue a minimum of 275 billion pesetas in three and 10-year bonds and 200 billion in five and 15-year bonds. This is close to the 466 billion the Treasury sold at the auctions in September.
But the real appointment, dealers said, is coming on Thursday when the next Bank of Spain repo should give an official imprimatur to the 1997 budget.
The market has already discounted a 50 basis point rate cut in the money market official rate, dealers said, and it could be disappointed if the Bank of Spain isn't that generous.
